what_it_does: Joint communication-and-sensing systems (like radar that doubles as wireless data link, following the IEEE 802.11ay standard) need local oscillators that can hop between frequencies extremely fast—in less than 18 nanoseconds. Additionally, these oscillators must suppress spurious tones (unwanted frequency components) to avoid breaking sensitive sensors. This paper describes a 60GHz oscillator using a single-sideband mixer topology with an integrated filter, achieving both ultra-fast frequency switching (sub-nanosecond settling) and extremely clean output (spurs suppressed to -56dBc, meaning spurious noise is thousands of times weaker than the main signal).
